newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line sees substantial lift in '97.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line sees substantial lift in '97.

text.p: Stena Line's chief executive, Bo Lerenius, on Thursday said the Swedish ferry operator's result would improve substantially next year after posting a loss in 1996, forecast to come in at about 450 million crowns.

"We will improve substantially next year," Lerenius told Reuters after Stena Line posted a loss after financial items of 251 million crowns for the first nine months of 1996 against a profit of 272 million crowns a year ago.
"I think there will be a big improvement in profits next year from the present result."

Stena Line in its nine month report repeated an earlier forecast for a loss of around 450 million crowns for calendar 1996. For 1995 the company posted a profit after financial items of 201 million crowns.
Asked if 1997 would see the company return to profit, Lerenius said: "I am not willing to comment on that yet publicly."

Lerenius blamed the losses in 1996 to two factors: reduced freight tonnage volumes due to the delayed delivery of two ferries in the Irish Sea, and the price war against the Eurotunnel on the English Channel.

"We have now decided to defend out position on the Dover-Calais route (which accounts for 25 percent of Stena's turnover)," Lerenius said, referring to a merger on three Channel routes with Britain's P&O announced earlier this month.
He said once official approvals were received for the merger it would boost Stena Line.
Stena Line shares weakened in morning trade, slipping 0.9 crowns to 28.10 by 1030 GMT.
